items.summary: Airport jobs at Changi, including baggage handling, are attracting local job seekers in Singapore, but hiring remains difficult. Recruitment platform FastJobs reported close to 600 applicants for the roles, with roughly six in ten being Singaporeans and permanent residents. FastJobs founder Julian Tan said demanding duties may cause drop-offs before work begins. The recruitment challenge follows a Ministry of Manpower investigation into suspected Employment Pass misuse involving around 45 companies and about 270 workers at ground handler SATS' contractors.
items.title: Changi Airport Baggage Jobs Draw Locals as Hiring Stays Hard

items.summary: On Nov 5, Wall Street’s Cboe Volatility Index logged its biggest intraday jump in more than 18 months after the Nasdaq 100 index fell 6.4%, erasing US$2.5 trillion (S$3.2 trillion) in market value. The selloff followed Democrats’ midterm victory, with traders worried AI infrastructure expansion could stall and demand for protection surging as put premiums ran at about two times typical levels. Analysts said much of the selling reflected an unwind of a crowded AI trade rather than a lasting shift; hedge funds were down 2.6% from a year earlier on large tech exposure. The article notes uncertainty over whether this re-evaluation is secular or just a trading rebalance, leaving markets to watch investor sentiment closely.
items.title: Wall Street fear gauge soars as AI trade faces midterm uncertainty

items.summary: Google released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, its newest video generation and editing model, generally available on Google Cloud and the Gemini API as of June 3. The version generates and edits clips up to 15 seconds natively, a step up from 10 seconds in Omni 1.1. Its price drops about 30% to $0.07 per second of 720p video, roughly $1.05 for a full clip; the prior version billed around $0.10 per second at that resolution. Google reports better reference adherence and less drift but has not published benchmark scores for 1.2, resting its claims on side-by-side demos against Omni 1.1. Early partner feedback is positive but self-selected.
items.title: Google Releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: 15-Second AI Video at $0.07 per Second

items.summary: Hackers are using fake OpenAI, SpaceX, and Anthropic event invitations to lure employees into phishing attacks. According to a new report from Push Security, attackers use convincing registration pages offering free premium AI services to trick victims into signing in with corporate accounts. The same pages integrate two PhaaS platforms—Kali365 for Microsoft device code phishing and VoidProxy as an adversary-in-the-middle proxy to steal Google session cookies. Push Security detected and blocked visits to the malicious pages in late October 2026.
items.title: Push Security Warns of Fake AI Event Phishing Attacks

items.summary: An independent monitoring group, Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), released an analysis Thursday stating that Anthropic is developing its artificial intelligence systems around twice as quickly as a year earlier. METR estimated the company improved model capabilities for well-specified tasks roughly double the prior rate. The findings emerge amid CEO Dario Amodei's September 12 essay urging slower AI improvement, and concern over models potentially eluding human control.
items.title: Independent Group Finds Anthropic's AI Development Doubled Despite Slowdown Calls

items.summary: Databricks published an online builder's guide explaining how to scale Databricks Apps, which it describes as running apps built on Python or Node.js. The article states that good scaling decisions begin before any code is written and walks readers through four stages: design, build, test and deploy, and operate. It focuses primarily on application performance and resiliency at scale rather than deployment automation. Using a retailer example in which 200 store managers use an app during Black Friday, the guide estimates query rates to illustrate load planning. Databricks recommends turning on telemetry from the start, writing async code for I/O-heavy work, keeping session state recoverable through soft and hard state splits, running load tests before production with tools such as Locust, and choosing instance sizes starting with Medium so measurements decide capacity rather than adding compute by default. The guide notes that Databricks Apps offers Medium, Large and XLarge instances and suggests at least two instances for higher availability.
items.title: Databricks publishes a builder's guide to scaling its Apps platform

items.summary: Aircraft engine turbines contain single crystal blade sections grown rather than cut, a process perfected in only five countries including the US and UK. Rolls-Royce's Ben Fifoot describes manufacturing it as complicated as possible while China aims to become the sixth nation to master the technology chain. In September GE Aerospace announced plans to acquire its turbine blade supplier for $11.75bn (£8.78bn), a move described as securing supply, and in March Rolls-Royce said it would invest more than £19m in its Rotherham casting facility.
items.title: Rolls-Royce engineers grow turbine blades that fight physics

items.summary: Anthropic is keeping Claude ad-free, a pledge from its Super Bowl commercial that its IPO filing did not even mention reversing. The company notes it can afford this with about $112 billion in investor cash. Meanwhile, competitors are embracing ads: OpenAI reports over 100,000 customers advertising in ChatGPT since February, and Google expanded AI Mode ads to 10 more countries beyond the US last week. Koah Labs, an ad tech startup reaching about 200 apps, says users click on about 3 percent of its ads—roughly matching Google’s performance—as chatbot advertising grows.
items.title: Anthropic Stays Ad-Free While Chatbot Ads Spread

items.summary: The FBI and CISA warn that hackers are actively targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems worldwide, potentially causing food spoilage, equipment damage, and fire hazards. The warning was issued jointly with the U. S. Departments of Health and Human Services, Agriculture, and Transportation, urging critical infrastructure operators to secure vulnerable controllers used in healthcare, food production, chemical facilities, and transportation. CISA's Chris Butera said every organization depending on these systems should assume it could be a target.
items.title: FBI and CISA Warn of Cyberattacks on Refrigeration Systems Worldwide

items.summary: Philippe Jaenada, who won France’s Prix Goncourt on Tuesday for L’Inconnue du quai de Javel, told France Inter radio that he had used artificial intelligence “three times” while writing it. His admission follows the Académie Goncourt removing Thélyson Orélien’s debut from its longlist after AI-detection software flagged much of it as machine-generated; Orélien called the allegations slander and denied using a machine, though his publisher later distanced itself. Jaenada said he would “acknowledge” and “tame” AI rather than hide it.
items.title: Goncourt winner admits using AI in his novel

items.summary: Airbnb announced Thursday that its custom-built AI travel agent will launch in the first half of 2027, citing CEO Brian Chesky's view that general-purpose chatbots fall short for trip planning. The company said the agent draws on a library of travel-specific interface components and nearly two decades of hosting experience. News came alongside strong Q3 earnings, with revenue up 19% to $4.87 billion.
items.title: Airbnb Commits AI Travel Agent Launch to First Half of 2027

items.summary: After a nationwide setback for their party and President Donald Trump, Florida's Republican Party narrowly held statewide races Tuesday while losing congressional seats and legislative super-majorities. Byron Donalds won governorship over David Jolly by just over 1 percent; Ashley Moody took the Senate seat under Angie Nixon by less than 3 percent. Both GOP candidates raised far more money, and Republicans boast 1.5 million more registered voters. Democrats kept four redrawn congressional seats and gained legislative influence. Analyst Aubrey Jewett noted a loss still stings but may give Democrats hope; Susannah Randolph called the redistricting effort failed and suggested Florida could swing again; Rachel Cleetus linked heavy rain flooding to climate change urgency, quoting that such issues are top-of-mind for voters.
items.title: Florida Republicans Hold Narrowly After National Democratic Wave

items.summary: Analysis by Lauri Myllyvirta of the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, published via Carbon Brief, reports China's carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions fell 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, the largest quarterly decline since the 2022 Covid lockdowns. Coal use dropped 3% year-on-year while oil fell 4%. The trend extends a flat or falling pattern from March 2024.
items.title: China's CO2 emissions hit largest quarterly drop since Covid lockdowns

items.summary: Australian conversion specialist Janus Electric has secured a battery supply agreement with Electrovaya for its Class 8 electric truck conversions, which replace diesel engines with swappable battery power. The deal includes an initial purchase order of $26 million in batteries and Electrovaya buying approximately $1.4 million worth of Janus stock. Ben Hutt, Managing Director and CEO of Janus Electric, said the investment signals confidence in their technology as reliable battery supply is critical to growth. Dr. Raj Das Gupta, CEO of Electrovaya, noted that Class 8 trucking remains a demanding frontier for electrification. The trucks carry a 480 hp motor drawing from a 310 kWh pack, offering up to 370 miles and four-minute battery swaps.
items.title: Janus Electric Signs Battery Supply Deal With Electrovaya

items.summary:
U.S. oil prices rebounded Thursday after Democrats took control of the House and Senate, raising expectations for a legislative check on Trump's administration. Brent rose 4% to $98.38 per barrel at 3:15 pm ET, while WTI gained 2.9% to $90.65. The S&P 500 fell more than 3% and the Nasdaq about 5%, as a selloff in AI chip stocks intensified after Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Texas Governor Greg Abbott. Earlier Wednesday's 8.7% Brent plunge had priced bets on Iran peace talks; those faded Thursday, with Eurasia Group cutting agreement odds to 10%. Separately, Sunrun shares climbed 13.3% to $9.96 after reporting revenue of $1.10 billion, up 52%, against estimates of $757.53 million.

By Alex Kimani for Oilprice.com
items.title: Oil Rises as Democratic Gains Shake Energy and AI Stocks

items.summary: German forklift maker Jungheinrich is launching a new line of electric counterbalance forklifts aimed at the region’s tight warehouses and factories. The next-generation EFG MB and MC models offer two performance packages, with higher-performance versions rated 2.5-3.0 tons and lead-acid or lithium-ion batteries of 346 or 690 Ah capacity. Buyers can add capabilities as needs grow. Lisa Jing Xue, Managing Director at Jungheinrich’s Qingpu Plant in China, said customers could configure trucks around their application and workload. Order books for both three- and four-wheel models are open now, backed by the company’s service network of 6,000+ people across Asia-Pacific.
items.title: Jungheinrich Unveils New Forklift Line for Asian Markets

items.summary: The largest U.S. shale producers have kept capital spending on drilling conservative this year even as the average WTI crude price rose about $20 per barrel, averaging $86.72 versus a 2025 average of $64.94. Diamondback Energy signaled it will not materially increase drilling next year amid global uncertainty, with chief executive Kaes Van't Hof citing downside risk and unpredictable oil supply normalization. Wood Mackenzie's Nathan Nemeth says smaller independents are more inclined to drill more, while larger operators remain cautious about volatile prices. Supermajor ExxonMobil is likewise focused on efficient execution rather than volume targets.
items.title: Big U.S. shale firms hold drilling despite higher oil prices

items.summary: Potential investors in Anthropic's planned initial public offering are raising doubts about whether the company can proceed with its roadshow next week for a November listing, four people familiar with investor discussions told Reuters. Investors want a more attractive valuation than the $1.5 trillion figure some had discussed and may demand a larger discount given the startup's record quarterly losses. Anthropic declined to comment on the doubts. The concerns come amid the sharpest technology stocks selloff in a year following Tuesday's US midterm elections, with AI-related assets under heavy pressure. A delay could weigh on broader market sentiment as large technology firms carry much of its weight.
items.title: Investor Doubts Threaten Anthropic IPO Timing

items.summary: On Thursday, Anthropic announced it is rolling out a personal finance feature for its Claude chatbot to paid subscribers this week. The tool lets users link accounts via Plaid and ask about balances, spending, and bills. Access is read-only.
items.title: Anthropic Rolls Out Personal Finance Feature for Claude in Beta

items.summary: Fears that an incoming Democratic Congress would tighten AI rules sparked a sharp selloff in tech stocks two days after the midterms, sending the Nasdaq down more than 5% and wiping out over $2 trillion in market value. The Dow Jones and S&P also fell. Investors worry about data centers gobbling water and energy, though companies like Meta and Alphabet still need them to develop AI.
items.title: AI Regulation Fears Trigger $2 Trillion Tech Rout

items.summary: Several people shared uncomfortable interview experiences with the BBC, prompted by a story on an awkward question. Tiara Allen waited about 40 minutes for her interviewer; Chas Edwards was hired after saying he did not cry, then worked there 13 months before leaving. Corinne Mills of Personal Career Management suggested asking interviewers to clarify odd questions and noted candidates can judge firms too. Employment lawyer Roy Magara said some biased questions are illegal, such as those about children or age.
items.title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

items.summary: Pasture mealybugs, an invasive insect that is difficult to detect and eliminate, have killed large areas of grasses across the Southeast. Experts warn it poses a multi-billion dollar threat to agriculture, adding pressure on farmers already facing high costs.
items.title: Invasive Pasture Mealybug Threatens Southeast Grasslands and Farmers

items.summary: Experts say Democratic wins in US midterm elections are unlikely to soften Washington's tariff and trade stance, though they may give India some reprieve on the bilateral trade deal. Analysts note that Trump's tariffs from January 2025 probably will not be fully reversed, but negotiations could offer India more room.
items.title: US Midterm Elections Unlikely to Change Tariff Equation for India

items.summary: Business Today profiles women leaders across eyewear, quick commerce, genomics and defence electronics who are turning early ideas into scaled companies. Neha Bansal of Lenskart built a technology-led eyewear business; Nandita Sinha took over Swiggy's Instamart in August 2026; Anuradha Acharya brought Mapmygenome closer to consumers; Rekha Murthy Rangarajan developed manufacturing at Data Patterns, which grew from about 45 employees to around 1,700. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation reported women's managerial positions rose 102.54% between 2017 and 2025 versus a 73.8% rise for men. An AIMA–KPMG report from 2026 surveyed more than 200 professionals, finding 55% have a defined leadership-assessment process but only 28% see it as fair. The leaders stress building processes and credibility rather than relying on gender alone.
items.title: Women Leaders Build India's New-Age Businesses

items.summary: Following Democratic gains in the US midterm elections, Ukraine welcomed prospects of a more sympathetic Washington and hoped for greater support. Analysts suggested this could shift Russia's strategic calculations toward the West. Kyiv's leader expressed hope for increased backing, while reports indicated Moscow might intensify its aerial assault if Trump weakens.
items.title: Ukraine Hopes for Increased US Support After Midterm Elections

items.summary: The Guardian reviewed Elif Shafak's new book, In One Brief Moment All Eternity. It describes a scene in which the character Emma Bovary speaks to Gustave Flaubert while he writes, drawing in 30 women from his life. The reviewer calls it an audacious novel and says its narrative invention becomes a kind of bravura performance as unexpected connections emerge.
items.title: Guardian calls Shafak's Flaubert novel audacious and inventive

items.summary: The single-sentence item is a caption for a Ben Jennings political cartoon, not an article with findings or figures. It names the cartoonist and its subject — wealthy people who supported Donald Trump — without stating any event, data, quote, or claim beyond that description.
items.title: Ben Jennings cartoon on billionaires who backed Trump

items.summary: Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, testified at his New South Wales Supreme Court trial for the alleged February 2024 murders of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies. He described a fatal confrontation with both men, said he dressed as an UberEats rider to retrieve belongings without contact, signed out his firearm three days earlier, and pleaded not guilty to two murder counts plus aggravated break-and-enter.
items.title: Former officer testifies in NSW double murder trial

items.summary: Donald Trump signed a proclamation Thursday declaring the gold-covered Oval Office and Cabinet Room national monuments to prevent future administrations from altering his design. He said it would make them landmarks for the ages, untouched by anyone. The move follows midterm election losses and comes amid ongoing White House renovation projects drawing criticism.
items.title: Trump Signs Proclamation Protecting Gold-Covered Oval Office Design

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV has begun a lengthy trip across Uruguay, Argentina and Peru just three weeks after undergoing surgery to remove a tumour from his right lung. The Vatican says no extraordinary measures are being taken for his health, describing him as a 71-year-old who had an operation rather than someone with a permanent medical condition. He revealed last month that the growth was found during a routine scan and confirmed it had not spread. A spokeswoman stressed he has "fantastic stamina" and is "extremely enthusiastic" about the schedule he personally confirmed. The 12-day tour, covering thousands of miles from the Amazon to the Andes, includes his anticipated return to Peru where he served as a priest for nearly 20 years.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV begins Latin America tour weeks after lung surgery

items.summary: Japanese nominal wages rose 4.6% year-on-year in September, the labor ministry reported Friday, marking the largest gain since 1997 and the fastest pace in almost three decades. Base pay climbed 3.7%, while a gauge excluding bonuses, overtime and sampling distortions rose by a record 3.1% for full-time workers. Real cash earnings accelerated to 2.2% from a revised 1.6% gain in August, beating consensus estimates of 1.3%. The strength supports the Bank of Japan’s plan to hike rates as soon as December.
items.title: Japan’s Wages Rise at Fastest Pace in Nearly Three Decades

items.summary: Nithya Raman, a democratic socialist and city council member, defeated incumbent mayor Karen Bass in the Los Angeles mayoral race. Her victory surprised observers after she entered as a long-shot candidate against Bass, who had never lost an office bid. Bass conceded on Thursday, saying 'the people of Los Angeles have spoken.' The win adds to progressive leadership gains in major US cities.
items.title: Democratic Socialist Nithya Raman Defeats Karen Bass for LA Mayor

items.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told parliament on Friday that the government was watching market developments carefully as volatility from US mid-term elections affected economies globally. She noted share prices in AI and chip sectors were falling sharply, then said Japan would focus on creating a strong economy by strengthening industries where it holds competitive advantage.
items.title: Japan PM Takaichi Vows Economic Focus Amid Market Turbulence

items.summary: U. S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed Thursday reports that he planned to leave the Trump administration as he considers his next steps after Republican midterm losses, according to The New York Times. In an interview, Rubio said it has always been his plan to serve until the end of Trump's term and declined further questions about 2028, telling reporters: "I literally will not talk about 2028 anymore." Earlier Thursday, Bloomberg News reported he was weighing leaving after speaking with White House officials.
items.title: Rubio Denies Reports of Exit for White House Bid

items.summary: As the Rugby League World Cup reaches its semi-finals, an analysis of the four remaining squads finds that although Pacific nations feature prominently, most players were actually born in Australia or New Zealand. The authors report 85% for the women’s competition and 95% for the men. They note deep migration ties across the region, small island populations reaching success despite tiny sizes, and a comparatively youthful Pacific population offering what they call a demographic dividend that requires investment to realise. The piece frames these patterns as reflecting family connections and sporting opportunities rather than any single cause.
items.title: Pacific rugby league squads are mostly born in Australia and New Zealand

items.summary: Sand exports from Cambodia to Singapore have resumed after a nine-year ban, with Cambodian trade statistics showing more than 694,000 tons of sand worth $3.47 million exported between June and September 2026. Mining is underway along the Trapeang Rung River in Koh Kong province, an area conservationists describe as having “astonishing” biodiversity. Fishers at the village of Koh Sralao say dredging has blocked access to fishing grounds and damaged their catch; one resident reported oil slicks that could harm ecosystems for long periods. The operation runs near protected areas including a Ramsar wetland just 3 km downstream, prompting calls from conservationists and politicians for greater transparency in Singapore's sand sourcing. Mongabay noted it could not obtain Singapore's official import data for the period, though ship tracking suggests exports show no signs of slowing.
items.title: Cambodia's Sand Exports Resume Amid Fishing Community Fears

items.summary: The British version of Married At First Sight was cancelled after a review launched over sexual assault allegations. The BBC's Channel 4 removed all previous seasons in May. The broadcaster said implementing the review's recommendations would change the show's format, and it had run its course after 10 years.
items.title: Channel 4 Cancels UK Married At First Sight After Review Over Rape Allegations

items.summary: Governor Gavin Newsom has moved to grant clemency to all 548 people sentenced to death in California, according to his office. About 382 of those commutations would require approval from the state's Supreme Court, which he said represented roughly 70 per cent and is likely to be mixed. In a letter, Mr Newsom called it one of the most difficult decisions of his career after eight years in office as he weighs a presidential run. Critics including Crime Survivors founder Patricia Wenskunas called it offensive, while the ACLU applauded it. The California District Attorneys Association has yet to comment.
items.title: Newsom Moves Toward Clemency for All California Death Row Inmates

items.summary: In al-Mughayyir, an occupied West Bank village of around 3,000 people with roughly 4,300 hectares of land, Palestinian families harvested olives during a few permitted days while soldiers stood guard and fired tear gas. Residents say they can access barely 100 hectares despite needing year-round care for their trees. Across the West Bank, the UN recorded 377 settler attacks since September, leaving one dead, more than 200 injured and 3,850 trees damaged.
items.title: Palestinians Harvest Olives Under Israeli Military Restrictions in West Bank

items.summary:
Political scientist Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's 2026 U.S. Senate race, though his support among Black voters fell short of that of other Democratic candidates. He trailed Haley Stevens in the August primary and received about 70.6% of Wayne County votes versus Kamala Harris's 62.7% in 2024. El-Sayed drew roughly equal Black voter support to moderate Democrat Elissa Slotkin, yet his progressive platform and lack of governing experience may have deterred some voters who value experience. Statewide estimates put his Black support near 86%, below Governor Whitmer's about 94% in 2022 and Jocelyn Benson's 90%. The author notes early results cannot confirm whether Black voters embraced the progressive agenda or simply backed a Democrat, so close races remain sensitive to turnout shifts. A Detroit voter quoted ABC News as saying Haley Stevens "pimped my community" after her last-minute endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers.

visual null },
items.title: Michigan Black Voters Backed El-Sayed but Less Enthusiastically Than Peers

items.summary: Speaking to Spanish, Portuguese and Latin American leaders, Zelensky appealed for transformers, power cables, generators and electronic equipment to restore infrastructure damaged by Russian attacks. He named Brazil, Mexico, Argentina and Colombia as potential transformer suppliers, Chile for cables and Spain for electrical gear. Ukraine requires compatible supplies and direct manufacturer contacts.
items.title: Zelensky Urges Latin America for Ukraine Power Grid Repair Supplies

items.summary: President Santiago Peña resigned Thursday after the collapse of Ueno Bank, a digital lender tied to his government that froze millions of savings. Minutes later, the lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, sending charges to the Senate; congressional leaders expected to accept his resignation so Vice President Pedro Alliana could be sworn in without waiting for a trial, though opposition senators still demanded one. Peña apologized but declined full responsibility as depositors and retirees scrambled over frozen funds. The guaraní fell nearly 4% against the dollar Thursday, reaching about 7% weekly losses. Ueno had claimed more than 60% of adults as customers before regulators seized it Tuesday after finding risky insider lending that left its capital below half the legal minimum; prosecutors charged 27 officials with breach of trust and attempted fraud while six executives face detention.
items.title: Paraguay's President Resigns and Is Impeached After Bank Collapse

items.summary: In Tuesday's midterm elections, voters overwhelmingly rejected data center projects at the ballot box; of 41 referendum votes on such projects across 10 states, only one passed, per a Ballotpedia report. The Democratic Party's decisive victory has opened what analysts call a more challenging landscape for AI and technology industries in Washington. Critics accuse developers of raising electricity bills, consuming excessive water in drought-prone areas, lacking permitting transparency, and fueling NIMBY movements. Ohio alone saw 21 projects fail to secure approval; its new Democratic governor Amy Acton supports a moratorium until operators cover public-service costs. UBS estimates up to 30% of planned U.S. capacity by 2028 could face delays or disruptions, while Texas aims to become the world's largest data center market by 2030.
items.title: Midterm Voters Reject Data Center Expansion Across U.S.

items.summary: In the occupied West Bank village of al-Mughayyir, Palestinian families harvested their crops during one of the few days permitted by Israeli military approval. Residents say they can access barely 100 hectares of the roughly 4,300-hectare land, and such brief visits are insufficient to maintain trees needing year-round care. The village has faced settler pressure, with six residents killed in 2026 and around 12,000 olive trees uprooted from its eastern plain in 2025.
items.title: Palestinians harvest olives amid military restrictions in al-Mughayyir

items.summary: After his party lost the recent US midterm elections, President Donald Trump conceded that the Iran conflict may have hurt him politically. Observers note presidents who become lame ducks often turn to foreign policy as they consider their legacy. Analysts warn Iran could widen its targets and Gulf states face renewed attacks while seeking a political off-ramp. Experts like Ross Harrison of MEI say regional security cooperation with Tehran is inevitable, though Ryan Crocker doubts near-term Gulf unity. Andreas Krieg argues Trump's lame-duck status may accelerate the region's move toward strategic autonomy from Washington.
items.title: Gulf States Brace for Possible US-Iran War Renewal After Trump's Midterm Defeat

items.summary: Potential investors want a more attractive valuation before committing to Anthropic's offering, with some viewing the recently discussed $1.5 trillion figure as high, people told Reuters. A sharp selloff in technology stocks and geopolitical uncertainty weigh on new offerings. Anthropic declined to comment. Analysts say strong retail demand could still help; one partner said such firms will become public despite a likely private-market pullback.
items.title: Anthropic IPO May Slip as Investors Seek Lower Valuation

items.summary: A guide published ahead of Dhanteras, the festival opening India's five-day Diwali celebrations on Friday, 6 November. It explains what the day observes—worship of Lakshmi, Dhanvantari and Kubera—and offers a ready-to-use collection of wishes, messages, quotes, image captions and WhatsApp status lines for family, friends, colleagues and loved ones abroad. Readers are invited to tweak them, use only their own or freely usable images, and buy valuables from trusted sellers while keeping receipts. The piece notes that puja timings vary by region and panchang, adds a disclaimer that it is informational only and offers no financial advice, and frames the quotes as original suggestions for personal sharing.
items.title: Dhanteras Wishes and Status Lines for Diwali's Opening Festival

items.summary: The BSE total market capitalization crossed Rs 500 lakh crore after 622 trading sessions from the April 8, 2024 level of Rs 400 lakh crore. The rise followed strong IPO activity in 2024-2026 and was supported by a crude oil price decline of more than 19% over three sessions and foreign inflows exceeding $3.4 billion in 12 sessions, though several benchmark indices remain below their peaks.
items.title: BSE market cap crosses Rs 500 lakh crore on IPOs and recovery

items.summary: NSDL and CDSL added nearly 3.36 million demat accounts in October, the highest monthly total since January 2026. The overall count reached around 244 million by month-end, though this includes investors holding multiple accounts; unique investors are estimated at about 136.6 million as of September per NSE data. Strong IPO activity drove the rise: 13 issues raised a record ₹44,507 crore in October, including Jio Platforms' largest-ever offering. Sunny Agrawal of SBICAP Securities noted that account openings typically climb with surging IPOs.
items.title: Demat account additions reach nine-month high in October

items.summary: The BJP accused the Indian National Congress and other opposition figures of planning unrest following an undercover broadcast by Times Now Navbharat titled Operation Regime Change. BJP spokesman Gaurav Bhatia said the hidden-camera conversations exposed alleged attempts at regime change outside democratic process, warning of violent protests and Nepal-like events. The channel noted that not all participants supported violence or rejected such possibilities. Congress demanded concrete evidence before accepting the allegations.
items.title: BJP accuses opposition of plotting unrest after TV sting

items.summary: The Indian Youth Congress suspended more than 300 office-bearers across 12 states for missing the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Delhi' rally on Nov 1 and failing to log attendance. Chief Uday Bhanu Chib said around 20,000 workers attended but discipline was essential in serious times. Suspended members may be reinstated if they perform well later; MP led suspensions with over 60, followed by Rajasthan's 32.
items.title: Indian Youth Congress suspends 300 office-bearers over rally no-shows

items.summary: Life insurer LIC reported a net profit of ₹12,076 crore, up about 20% year-on-year. Net premium income rose 16.2% to ₹1.47 lakh crore and net investment income reached ₹1.15 lakh crore from ₹1.12 lakh crore. Value of new business grew 33.95% to ₹6,846 crore in H1 FY27. Ajay Kumar Srivastava noted MTM losses weighed on results while embedded value rose about 1%. LIC's Indian Embedded Value fell 1.95% due to equity market fluctuations.
items.title: LIC Posts 20% Profit Jump on Higher Premiums Amid Market Downturn

items.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed confidence that a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine could be reached soon, describing it as a “big, beautiful agreement” that might involve all of Europe. Speaking at the White House on November 6, 2026, he praised First Lady Melania Trump’s humanitarian work in facilitating communication and child reunifications. He also confirmed meeting Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev without disclosing details.
items.title: Trump Says Russia-Ukraine Peace Deal May Involve All of Europe Soon

items.summary: Nithya Raman won the Los Angeles mayoral election, defeating incumbent Karen Bass in races that concluded on November 3. Her victory extends a wave of Democratic Socialist gains led by Zohran Mamdani’s win as New York mayor last year. The organisation backing her voted 14-13 to continue its endorsement after an internal debate over her position on Palestine and BDS, which had nearly ended support two days before the election. Raman centred her campaign on housing and city services under the slogan “A City That Works.” Membership reportedly rose from 6,500 in 2014 to 130,000 recently. Members now consider a national presidential campaign for Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez in 2028.
items.title: Raman’s LA Win Extends Democratic Socialist Momentum

items.summary: Viral Bhatt, founder of Money Mantra, advises salaried individuals to treat a Diwali bonus as hard-earned money rather than free money. He suggests short-term goals (up to three years) favour bank fixed deposits and high-quality fixed-income options over equity funds or debt mutual funds due to liquidity needs and market risk. Medium-term goals may suit conservative hybrid mixes, while long-term horizons can justify diversified equity funds for those tolerating volatility. Bhatt also recommends reviewing EPF and PPF savings before investing, prioritising essential obligations like insurance premiums and EMIs over festive spending, and avoiding five common mistakes: overspending on lifestyle items, excessive credit-card use, herd behaviour, chasing past returns, and neglecting emergency savings and insurance.
items.title: Money Mantra Founder Urges Cautious Handling of Diwali Bonus

items.summary: This fact-check article examines Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's projected image of the state as a leading Indian growth story, concluding that his assertions on industrialisation, incomes and job creation are patchy. The authors note agriculture still marginally edges manufacturing in GSDP while per-capita income stays low, and flag an implementation gap: over Rs 45 lakh crore in investment proposals versus only Rs 15 lakh crore implemented, with a declared Rs 50 lakh crore of new proposals unverified. Female labour force participation claims lack official sourcing and remain below the all-India average. The piece flags weak urbanisation, regional concentration around Noida-Greater Noida, de-industrialised Kanpur, power shortages and skills mismatches as further shortcomings, framing development as uneven with exaggerated leadership claims.
items.title: Fact-check finds gaps in Yogi Adityanath's UP growth claims

items.summary: Two young Indian drivers, Saishiva Sankaran and Viswas Vijayaraj, spoke to the Times of India at the return of the Indian Racing Festival to the Buddh International Circuit after 13 years. Both began racing in childhood karting and now compete in junior categories such as F2000 and the Indian Racing League while balancing school and family life. They describe limited testing opportunities for Indian drivers compared with international competitors, who practise almost every day whereas Indian racers get only a couple of days a month. Vijayaraj noted that financial backing remains a major hurdle on the road to Formula 1, which he calls always a dream. Sankaran aims to reach F1 next year and seeks sponsors, while also admiring Max Verstappen. Both believe capable Indian drivers already exist but need more national support.
items.title: Young Indian Racers Chase Formula 1 Dreams Amid Financial Hurdles

items.summary: Railway police arrested Rahul Soni, a 36-year-old resident of Howrah, after finding about Rs 1.40 crore in cash packed inside his bags at Platform 7 of Kharagpur Railway Station on Wednesday. The currency-counting machine confirmed the total as Rs 1.40 crore across 280 bundles of Rs 500 notes. Soni could not produce documents proving the money's legitimate source, so police seized it and registered Case No. 167/26 under Sections 317(2), 317(5) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; he reportedly said he was moving the cash from Tatanagar to Howrah.
items.title: Man Arrested With Rs 1.4 Crore Unaccounted Cash at Kharagpur Railway Station
